newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, new contract lows set.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, new contract lows set.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower and just above their new contract lows on overall bearishness about wheat, traders said.
"We're heading lower to get in line with increasingly competitive world values," one MGE floor source said.

U.S. wheat markets were undermined by talk of French wheat offered to Egypt at relatively cheap values. There was also mention of the EU's move to scrap a wheat export tax, as well as USDA's upwardly revised forecast of world wheat carryout.
But MGE sources said mill-buying helped limit some spring wheat losses.

Traders noted the premium that was bid for 15 percent proteins. On Friday, 15 percent protein spring wheat traded in Minneapolis at $1.25 over the MGE Dec contract, compared to 50 cents over for 14 percent.
MGE spring wheat closed 1-3/4 to seven cents per bushel lower, with Dec down seven cents per bushel at $4.13-1/2, just above the new contract low of $4.12-1/2.
Traders said LFG and Wilson Trading each sold one million Dec and bought 2.5 million Dec. Atwood-Peavey sold 1.5 million Dec and bought 1.5 million March, traders said.
MGE feed barley closed unchanged to 13 cents per hundredweight lower, with Dec down 13 cents at $7.31.
